chunks: And they say: 'Our hearts are enfolded in covers.' In fact God has cursed them for their unbelief; and only a little do they believe.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says 'Our hearts are enfolded in covers'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a response to the claim of the hypocrites (Munafiqun) that their hearts were naturally impervious to truth, whereas the Quran attributes the 'sealing' to their own active rejection and divine curse. The term 'ghulf' (sealed/covered) signifies a spiritual hardening resulting from persistent disbelief, rendering their faith minimal and fragile. This highlights the Shia understanding of the interplay between human agency in rejection and divine consequence in sealing the heart.
